id.description: Required stable id — used for `<label for>`, description, error, and the child control's id via context.

label.description: Visible label text. Omit only when the child control supplies its own accessible name, such as via aria-label or aria-labelledby.

labelVisible.description:
Whether the label is visibly rendered. Set `false` to visually hide it
while keeping it associated with the control.

description.description: Helper text rendered below the control; wired into `aria-describedby`.

warning.description: Advisory for a legal but potentially risky value; does not mark the control invalid.

error.description: Validation error; sets `aria-invalid="true"` on opted-in controls via context.

errorGlyph.description:
The glyph drawn before the error message: `warning` (a triangle, the default) for a value the
person can fix, or `error` (a circle) for a conflict such as a URL that is already connected.

note.description: Neutral explanation drawn under the helper text and wired into `aria-describedby`, such as why a field is cleared. Not an error and not a warning.

by.description: Policy or administrator that owns the value.

message.description: The whole line to show beside the lock glyph, replacing the "Managed by" wording, such as "Locked by your deployment (remote mode). Change it in the deployment's configuration."

managed.description: Policy ownership metadata displayed without disabling the control.

required.description: Renders a visual required marker and exposes `required: true` on the context.

disabled.description: Propagated to opted-in controls via context. Does not style FormField itself.

unsupportedProps.name: descriptionAction
unsupportedProps.description: Rendered after the helper text inside the same paragraph, so it joins `aria-describedby`: a quiet link such as "Where do I get one?". Shown only with `description`.

unsupportedProps.name: errorAction
unsupportedProps.description: Rendered after the error message inside the same live region, such as a link to the record that conflicts ("Open GitHub") or a quiet Retry.

unsupportedProps.name: trailing
unsupportedProps.description: Rendered beside the control on the same row, such as a Try again button after a failed test. The control takes the room the trailing content leaves.
